title: Polyglot event-envelope shims for streaming tool calls (TS / Py / Go)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver a lightweight, backward-compatible event envelope and small shim library across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs to unify streaming responses, function/tool call events, and structured outputs. The goal is to make cross-language integrations predictable: consumers can parse a single event stream and reliably detect tool invocation start/args, incremental token deltas, structured JSON emissions, and final metadata. This ticket scopes the interface design, in-repo examples, unit/integration tests, and a non-breaking rollout plan for hosted API users.
background: Current SDKs expose slightly different streaming shapes: TS has a framed stream of typed events, Python returns generator yields of mixed tuples, and Go exposes callback hooks with separate callbacks for tokens vs tool events. This has caused repeated client confusion and duplicated parsing logic in downstream infra (console, examples repo, community samples). We want a thin translation layer (event-envelope) that standardizes: event.type, event.id (optional), event.payload, event.schema (optional), and event.trace (optional). The shim should be opt-in initially (flagged feature) and have clear migration guidance.
acceptance_criteria: TS/Py/Go SDKs expose a stable EventEnvelope type documented in the SDK reference

End-to-end example: a single streaming connection yields a sequence of EventEnvelope objects covering: tool.invoke.start, tool.invoke.args, delta.token, structured.json.delta, tool.invoke.result, final.metadata
No breaking changes to existing high-level SDK APIs; the envelope is available as an alternate consumer API behind a small opt-in flag
Cross-language example app (chat + calculator tool) in repo/examples demonstrating identical parsing logic in TS/Py/Go
Unit tests covering ordering guarantees, partial JSON assembly, and tool-call failure paths
Performance regression < 3% added CPU overhead in streaming hot path (benchmarked)
api_proposals:
Python (sketch):

# simple dataclass representation
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional, Any

@dataclass
class EventEnvelope:
    id: Optional[str]
    type: str  # delta|tool|structured|final|error
    payload: Optional[Any] = None
    schema: Optional[str] = None
    trace: Optional[dict] = None

# consumer API
for event in client.stream(..., envelope=True):
    if event.type == 'delta':
        buffer.write(event.payload)
    elif event.type == 'tool':
        dispatch_tool(event.payload)

Notes: code sketches above are intentionally minimal; we will add typed helpers for incremental JSON assembly (structured events may emit partial JSON text in multiple events), and a small OrderedEventBuffer to guarantee reassembly when the stream may interleave deltas and tool frames.
migration_notes: Opt-in initially: SDK constructors will accept envelope=true. Existing streaming consumers not opting in see unchanged behavior.
Provide a compatibility helper `wrapLegacyStreamToEnvelope(stream)` for TS/Py to ease migration of older clients that parse tokens or tool frames separately.
Document common migration patterns in the SDK changelog and examples: building a chat UI with tool calls, and server-side reranker that inspects structured outputs.
Deprecation path: If adoption reaches 70% after 3 months, warn about turning on envelopes by default for new clients; any default change will be signposted with opt-out for 2 release cycles.
testing_plan: Unit tests: envelope serialization/deserialization (TS/Py/Go) including partial structured JSON assembly and error frames.
Integration: example app (examples/multipoly/envelope-chat) runs against a local integration server that emits mixed events and verifies final state matches expectations.
Performance: microbenchmarks for streaming hot path with envelope=true vs baseline; measure latency and CPU at 1k concurrent streams.
Chaos test: inject tool failures and out-of-order event fragments to validate reassembly logic and graceful failures.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): merge shims into 3 SDK repos behind feature flag; run examples in CI; invite internal teams (console, examples) to test for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (opt-in public): publish minor SDK releases with envelope opt-in; include migration docs and example apps in the release notes.
Phase 3 (monitor): track adoption via telemetry (envelope:1) and error spikes; address issues in 2-week cadence.
Phase 4 (default toggle decision): after metrics and community feedback, decide whether to flip default for new clients.

notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) Use a single event envelope vs separate typed streams — chose envelope for simpler consumer model and fewer open network connections. 2) Strict typing vs flexible payload: lean toward flexible payload with optional schema field to avoid frequent SDK releases when tool argument shapes change.

Open questions: how to version envelopes long-term (semantic envelope version header?), and whether to add a small binary framing layer for lower CPU cost on very high-throughput customers. Will follow up in design doc.
